Alpha-c re-check complete on batch 7. Both halves written; the closure gate now reads **8/8 reviewed, 0 insufficient, 0 unreviewed**.

## What I verified from disk in this dispatch

All four blocking findings are fixed, and the fixes are real:

| id | on disk |
|---|---|
| B7-1 | `cor-comonads-on-a-preorder-are-interior-operators` = A item 38 (immediately after item 37, as specified); `ex-the-interior-comonad-on-a-topological-space` = B item 7. Riehl 5.1.7 split into four rows, 5.2.6(iv) into two — each names an item that carries what it names |
| B7-2 | Cheng locator extended through Example 2.4; `ex-a-distributive-law-between-two-finite-closure-operator-monads` = B item 8, contract computes the witness *and* the composite |
| B7-3 | `ex-the-ultrafilter-monad-on-a-finite-set` = B item 10; `filters-and-ultrafilters-examples` in the B page's `requires` |
| B7-4 | `thm-monad-morphisms-on-a-fixed-category-form-a-category` = A item 32, immediately after `def-monad-morphism` |

**I opened three of the four source PDFs**, because B7-1, B7-2 and B7-4 each rested on a claim about what a source says — and B7-4's remedy rested on the one premise my step-3 review explicitly left to the Beta. Mac Lane p. 139 closes §VI.1: *"We leave the reader to describe a morphism … of monads … and the category of all monads in a given category X."* The Beta's source claim is true verbatim; option (a) was the right branch. Riehl 5.1.7 states the kernel-operator dual and the interior example verbatim, so the newly minted headings are faithful rather than invented. Cheng's Examples 2.3/2.4 match their headings, Theorem 2.5 is the declared stop, and Cheng's own *"the composite monad TS is the free ring monad"* confirms the premise of R-1's repaired decline reason.

A side benefit: both Riehl (*"is given by"*) and Mac Lane (*"precisely when"*) state the preorder characterisation biconditionally, so my B7-8 title repair is literature-derived, not just my own derivation.

## New finding, repaired — R-4

This is R-2's repair having introduced a transcription-order gap one layer down.

The gate was re-raising them out of my own unmutated verdict file, and the Beta declined to manufacture a second `applied` claim for work already done. The defect was mine: prose said "ready for splice" while the machine-readable attestation still said `insufficient`.

That flag is filtered out and never read — every non-flag argument is treated as a coverage file. The error was mine, it reproduces identically on batch 1, and the header comment is a doc bug worth a separate fix.

**Verdict: `sufficient` — ready for splice.** Two items carry forward for step 4, neither blocking: apply the two design amendments insertion-first/rename-second, and put every further addition on the B page (A is at 59 of 60).
